payload.effect_name: Many Labs 2's little cultural heterogeneity conclusion
payload.effect_claim: Across the Many Labs 2 samples and settings, exploratory comparisons showed little heterogeneity between WEIRD and less-WEIRD cultures.
payload.effect_claim_quote: Exploratory comparisons revealed little heterogeneity between Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic (WEIRD) cultures and less WEIRD cultures
payload.original_title: Many Labs 2: Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Samples and Settings
payload.original_authors: Richard A. Klein et al.
payload.original_journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
payload.replication_title: Methodological concerns underlying a lack of evidence for cultural heterogeneity in the replication of psychological effects
payload.replication_authors: Robin Schimmelpfennig et al.
payload.replication_target_quote: We only draw on ML2 here as an illustrative example, but other projects ... may share some of these issues.
payload.outcome_quote: using different operationalizations of culture slightly increased effect sizes but did not substantially alter the conclusions of Many Labs 2.
payload.review_note: Source-checked reanalysis, not an independent new-participant replication: Schimmelpfennig et al. explicitly reanalyze the existing Many Labs 2 (ML2) data and label their cultural-moderation analysis as a re-analysis. Thus all ML2 participants/data are reused; no new sample is claimed. The narrowly scored effect is ML2's conclusion of little WEIRD-versus-less-WEIRD cultural heterogeneity, and the later paper reports that alternate culture operationalizations did not substantially change that conclusion. Later field evidence is the supplied cached OpenAlex record W4403203719, primary_topic.field Psychology, topic Cultural Differences and Values. OpenAlex author-ID comparison finds no shared authors (8 later authors versus 99 original authors); participant independence is nevertheless inapplicable because the later paper explicitly reuses the full ML2 dataset. Current promoted-pair precheck found no exact DOI pair or same-work canonical version.
